question.text: The Aztecs, meanwhile, used this language, whose modern variety is still widely spoken today. The words "chipotle" and "axolotl" come from this language.
question.clue: Historians learned to write in this language at schools called calmecacs ("kahl-MAY-kahks").

swap.leadin: This empire engaged in ritualized "flower wars" with its neighbors.
swap.text: Identify this Mesoamerican empire whose capital was Tenochtitlan. They were defeated by Hernan Cortez.
swap.clue: The Stone of Tizoc was created by people in this empire, which achieved huge agricultural output by building artificial islands on swamps to create so-called "floating gardens" or chinampas.

question.text: The largest ball court ruins are found in this pre-Columbian Mayan city, whose main attraction is the Temple to Kukulkan, a massive stepped pyramid nicknamed "El Caudillo."
question.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

swap.leadin: They were centered at sites such as Tres Zapotes, San Lorenzo, and La Venta.
swap.text: Identify this earliest Meso-American civilization centered in Mexico, famous for its large stone heads.
swap.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

question.leadin: This "City of the Gods" is home to the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon.
question.text: Name this UNESCO World Heritage city that is spanned by the Avenue of the Dead. This grid city was abandoned in the seventh century.
question.answerHtml: Teotihuacán [do not accept, prompt on, or otherwise reveal “Tenochtitlán”]
question.clue: The decline of this city has been attributed to an increase in power of the "intermediate elites" by archaeologists such as Linda Manzanilla.

swap.leadin: Before the Aztecs, the Zapotecs lived in the present-day Mexican state of Oaxaca.
swap.text: The Zapotecs adopted this sport from the Olmecs. This sport was played with a solid rubber object, and the Aztecs may have used it to defuse conflicts and resolve disputes.
swap.clue: Participants in this activity attached thin stone heads resembling ax blades to heavy belts known as yokes.

question.leadin: This man's coronation is documented on the Stone of the Five Suns.
question.text: Name this Aztec Emperor, whose possible death by stoning during La Noche Triste ended his captivity under Hernan Cortes.
question.clue: Shortly after this man's death, his people assassinated the rearguard of an invading force in the Night of Sorrows massacre.

swap.text: The prisoners from these religious wars were used for human sacrifice, and during them, the Aztecs fought neighboring city states such as the Tlaxcala.
swap.clue: This conflicts between Cholula, Texcoco, and other cities for the purpose of obtaining sacrifices.

question.text: Large numbers of children from this ethnic group were abducted after massacres carried out by forces loyal to Efrain Rios Montt in Guatemala. Rigoberta Menchu, a member of this indigenous group, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.
question.answerHtml: Maya [accept K'iche' Maya; prompt on indigenous peoples or Native Americans or Indians]
question.clue: A revolt of these people began a fifty-year long Caste War in the second half of the 19th century.

swap.leadin: Alberto Ruz Lhuillier (lweel-YAY) was buried at this site in honor of his work excavating it, and Jean-Frederic Maximilien de Waldeck supposedly lived on top of its Temple of the Count for three years while illustrating its ruins.
swap.text: Identify this city that flourished during the Late Classic Period. A tomb was found beneath the Temple of the Inscriptions at this site in 1952.
swap.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

question.leadin: Identify these pre-Columbian civilizations of the Americas.
question.text: This civilization founded a number of city-states in the Yucutan Peninsula, including Tikal and Chichen Itza.
question.clue: Pakal was one ruler of this civilization, which used cenotes (suh-no-tays) for the worship of their rain god.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about ancient Mesoamerican civilizations.
swap.text: The oldest known Mesoamerican civilization is this one, famous for its colossal stone heads that wear ballplayer helmets.
swap.clue: Archaeologists call its most significant city San Lorenzo, and one of its pyramids called Complex C is found in La Venta.

question.leadin: The supposedly "Ethiopian" features of these artworks led archaeologist Jose Melgar y Serrano to hypothesize that their makers had originated in Africa.
question.text: Name these artworks that depict men wearing protective helmets, found at sites like San Lorenzo and La Venta.
question.answerHtml: colossal heads [accept synonyms for colossal like large, titanic, enormous; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers like “Olmec heads”; prompt on just heads]

swap.leadin: One artifact from this civilisation was a jade mosaic mask of a "bat god"
swap.text: Identify this pre-Columbian civilisation which had its capital at Monte Alban. The first known artifact that includes this civilisation's writing is a danzante ("dahn-SAHN-tay") stone depicting a dead and bloodied man strung upside-down.
swap.clue: The golaba, bigana and coqui("KO-kee") were officials in this civilization, whose site of Lambityeco ("lam-bee-tee-ECK-oh") is home to depictions of its chief lightning god.

question.leadin: This figure reconquered Cozumel, following the failed attempt a year earlier by Juan de Grijalva and this figure's manipulation of the visit of five tax collectors to Zempoala set the tone for his greatest conquest.
question.text: Name this figure who won the Battle of Otumba against disorganized natives, after his lieutenant, Pedro de Alvarado, had thousands of nobles killed for worshipping Huitzilopochtli during the Toxcatl Massacre.
question.clue: The Florentine Codex details how this man's subordinate, Pedro de Alvarado, massacred most of the people at a festival in the Templo Mayor, leading to the retaliatory murder of this man's soldiers during La Noche Triste.

swap.text: The Southern Maya heartland contains potbelly architecture marked by large stone heads, similar to those of this much earlier civilization which had centers at La Venta and San Lorenzo.
swap.clue: Much of their art is based on a jaguar god, including much in that capital, La Venta.

question.text: This ceremonial center of the Mayan civilization is located in modern-day Guatemala, and features a notable Temple of the Jaguar.
question.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

swap.leadin: These two cities experienced a "Cold War," during which B'alaj Chan K'awiil established a military outpost at Dos Pilas.
swap.text: Name these two cities that fought three wars in the 6th through 8th centuries in the Peten Basin. Under "Ruler A," an ajaw from one of these cities defeated the other, leading Lady Six Sky to take power.

question.leadin: Even though all those damn Mesoamerican civilizations are pretty much the same, try to keep track of the one this bonus is asking about. FTPE.
question.text: Cosijo was the rain god of this civilization, which built cities at Mitla and Yagul and counted Cosijoeza among its kings.
question.clue: The chief god of this culture was the thunder god Cocijo.

swap.leadin: This historian's only written work was used by Tzevtan Todorov to argue that the "site of strategic symbolic occupation" was in the "body of a woman" that appeared in his major text.
swap.text: Name this man, who described how the Tlaxcala allied themselves with Hernan Cortes's expedition in his book The True History of the Conquest of New Spain.
